answer: FINAL ANSWER (concise, per submission contract): The distribution of the RNA expression data is HIGHLY RIGHT-SKEWED. On the raw (linear) scale of the COAD geneExp matrix, the pooled distribution has an adjusted Fisher–Pearson moment skewness g1 = +42.4 (Pearson's 2nd coefficient = +0.57; mean 932 ≫ median 177, right tail extending to ~1.34 million), and every one of the 328 samples is individually strongly right-skewed (per-sample g1 median ≈ +21). A log2(x+1) transform (sensitivity only) makes the distribution approximately symmetric (g1 ≈ −0.3), confirming the raw-scale skew comes from a heavy right tail of highly expressed genes, not from the transform choice.
